findings: GNU comm.c closes operands in order before totals, reporting fatal operand-close failures. Product closeOperand is called in that position.
Inputs.open returns one RecordReader for repeated stdin, but distinct readers for two opens of the same VFS pathname. No input refusal or alternate read cursor was added.
closeOperand checks caller cancellation, detects an already closed reader, and delegates to idempotent physical close. Final Inputs.close remains cleanup, not a second logical close.
readBytes ownership copy and record ordering/consumption code are unchanged; close errors occur after row consumption and before total output.
Producer/strict-order/output errors bypass the normal operand-finalization loop and retain their existing precedence; no native execution or dependency added to product.
limitations: Pinned GNU9.7 duplicate-stdin profile, not universal libc/GNU/BSD parity or a host descriptor implementation.
Cancellation cannot force uncooperative host work or undo effects; no filesystem capability or precision changes established.
